about: The pictures of promo edit 1, the Light. Every file was fetched from Wikimedia Commons on 2026-11-23 at the width given ('fetched_width'); 'licence' is what that page states. A statue's photograph is the museum's own, released CC0 under its Open Access policy (The Met's own record marks each isPublicDomain: true; 'museum_page' is that record). The icons and the painting are faithful photographs of flat works long out of copyright, marked Public domain on Commons. None is held in Greece or Italy (lib/marketing/heritagePictures.ts). 'eyes' is where the eyes are in the fetched file, read off by hand: the eye at the viewer's left first. The files themselves are out of git. From 2026-11-24, at his word that the pagans can be any kind of picture, the run also takes old engravings: flat printed works long out of copyright, marked Public domain on Commons. They are ink already and are not put through the ink filter. 'focus' is the point of the print that is held, as shares of its width and height. From his word of 2026-11-24 ("ensure its colored and western high quality art"), the run is Western paintings in colour. Each is long out of copyright and marked Public domain on Commons, though he said that need not hold for the pagans.
